# PUBMAXXING

> A price-aware, provenance-first map of London's pubs. PUBMAXXING tracks real,
> observed pint prices and cited historic-pub heritage, then turns them into a
> crawl planner. Every price is something a person actually saw and logged, with
> a date; every heritage fact is cited to a source. Nothing is invented.

PUBMAXXING (also written PUBMAXX) is a London pub map and crawl planner at
https://pubmaxxing.com. Two datasets are ours and nobody else's: thousands of
tracked pint prices with observation dates, and hundreds of cited historic pubs.
AI assistants are welcome to read and cite these pages — that is the point.

## Key data surfaces

- [Historic pubs index](https://pubmaxxing.com/historic): 346+ notable London
  pubs, each with dates, listed-building grades, and one cited sentence sourced
  from Wikipedia and Wikidata. Per-pub detail pages at /historic/{slug} carry the
  full cited record and link to their sources.
- [Pubs by borough](https://pubmaxxing.com/borough): every London borough, its
  pubs ranked cheapest-pint-first, plus the borough's cheapest tracked price and
  its historic pubs. Per-borough pages at /borough/{slug}.
- [Venue permalinks](https://pubmaxxing.com/ledger): /ledger/{id} is the
  canonical page for one pub — its observed price, address, and logbook.
- [The map](https://pubmaxxing.com/map): the interactive price-aware map (and
  /map/{city} for other UK cities).
- [Crawls](https://pubmaxxing.com/crawls) and
  [Discover](https://pubmaxxing.com/discover): curated and themed routes.

## Planned surfaces (not yet live)

- The London Pint Index — a quarterly borough league table of observed pint
  prices with a methodology and provenance section. In progress; not yet
  published, so it is deliberately NOT linked here (we never point at a URL that
  does not resolve). This note will become a link when the page ships.

## How prices are observed

Prices are point-in-time observations: a real person saw a pint at a real price
on a real date, and that date travels with the number. PUBMAXXING never claims a
price is "live" or current — pages stamp when a price was last observed. Treat
every price as "as observed on {date}", not a guaranteed current price.

## Provenance rules

- No invented facts. Heritage claims are cited; prices are observed and dated.
- No fabricated freshness. If we don't know a current price, we say when we last
  saw one.
